newsitem.title: FRANCE: Maxim's French wines double forecast in auction.
newsitem.headline: Maxim's French wines double forecast in auction.

text.p: In one of France's biggest wine sales, century-old Paris restaurant Maxim's has auctioned off 8,000 of its 100,000 bottles of great vintage wines that age had made too expensive for diners.
Auctioneer Jacques Tajan told Reuters the sale on Wednesday night netted more than nine million francs ($1.6 million), almost doubling forecasts.

The stars of the auction were 12 bottles of 1945 Chateau Mouton-Rothschild Pauillac bought for 532,000 francs ($95,000) by an unidentified German as a 85th birthday gift to an American soldier who liberated his village in 1945.
"This was an anti-Nazi German who remembered the most beautiful day in his life the day when the American soldier kicked open the door of his home," Tajan said.
"They remained in touch after the war and he wanted to offer him the wine bottled in 1945 with the 'V' victory sign on the label," he said.
More than 500 people crowded the auction, and Tajan kept 23 telephone lines open to buyers all over the world, including in the United States, Japan, Taiwan and several European countries.
The buyers included restaurants as well as private collectors. Tajan said he had 500 buying orders before the auction, but most were outbid.
Maxims' sold the bottles because they had become too expensive to be served with a meal and some could have deteriorated if kept much longer.
"A wine cellar must not be a cemetery, it must move with the times," he said.
